text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Greeek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos is arriving in Belgrade on Wednesday.
- Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic left on an official visit to Zimbabwe and Guinea.
- Two-day succession talks on the former Yugoslavia ended in Brussels with an agreement to continue the discussions in mid-November.
- Belgrade Jugobanka and Banco do Brasil agreed to cooperate and extend support to all Yugoslav and Brazilian firms needing banking aid in their business deals.
- Serbian industry minister Oskar Fodor received a delegation of the South Korean firm Samsung electronics and discussed joint investment projects in the production of digital telephone exchanges.
- The first GSM (Global System for mobile communications) exchange was opened in Belgrade Tuesday.
- Serbian oil industry (NIS) decides to reduce prices of motor oil, liquid gas oil and antifreeze by 20 percent. This is a seasonal reduction which will last to December 31.
- Yugoslav production has grown by 5.6 percent in the first nine months this year compared to the same period last year, according to the federal statistics office.
- Fifth international conference marking the 140th anniversary of the birth of famous scientist Nikola Tesla was opened in Belgrade.
NASA BORBA
- A delegation of the London club of creditor banks is arriving in Belgrade Wednesday, spokesman of Lowe Bell Financial, Yugoslavia's public relations adviser, said.
- Montenegrin seismologic experts announce possibility of strong earthquakes in Montenegro in the coming months.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic says the time of divisions is over.
- Belgrade Construction firm Partizanski Put signed a $12.5 million deal on building a 103 km road in Zambia.
POLITIKA EKSPRES

- The joint list of the ruling Socialist party of Serbia (SPS), Yugoslav united left (JUL) and New Democracy will win a more convincing victory than it had at previous elections, says SPS spokesman Ivica Dacic.
- First bus from Sarajevo arrives in Belgrade after four and a half years, broken links are now restored. Regular bus line to start operating from Thursday.
BORBA
- The consumer basket of main foods and beverages for a four member family is 1,264 dinars for September which is three percent higher than in August.
